Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

The new machine is the gray Dell tower beside the label printer, and it runs Windows 11. The uploader is called Parcel Bridge, version 4.8.2, and the account we are configuring is the shared Field Desk account, not my personal one. Please keep those names separate because the saved browser profile already has my own account in it. The archive folder is on the blue external drive labeled Field Archive, and that drive is mounted as F:\field archive on this machine. The incoming folder should be F:\field archive\incoming, and the completed folder should be F:\field archive\sent. The staging folder is already present as F:\field archive\staging, so don't create another one. The uploader window opens at 1280 by 800 on this monitor, and the scale setting is 125 percent. Leave both of those display values alone because the left side of the window is partly covered by the inventory panel.

For the connection profile, choose the office gateway rather than the travel gateway. The office gateway address is files.birchline.net, and the port is 443. The network team asked us to use the saved certificate named Birchline Office 2025 and not the generic system certificate. The timeout should be 45 seconds, and the retry count should be 3 attempts. Those are different settings; please don't treat 45 as a retry value. The upload limit is 680 megabytes for each file, and the daily account allowance is 12 gigabytes. Those numbers also have different roles. The team expects a single job to contain no more than 28 files, even when the account allowance has room for more. The file names must stay exactly as received because the archive index matches on the original names. If a file has spaces, retain them and don't replace them with underscores. For the suffix rule, allow PDF, TIF, and CSV files, and leave out temporary files ending in .part or .tmp. The sender field should read Field Desk Archive, and the reply address should remain archive@birchline.net.

The key I need you to check is written on its own line here:
transfer.allow_resume
It should be enabled so a dropped connection can continue from the last completed block rather than starting that file again, but only for files larger than 20 megabytes. For anything 20 megabytes or smaller, the uploader should start the file over if a connection drops. Do not apply the large file condition to the whole account or to the number of files in a job. The team tested the cutoff with a 19-megabyte scan and a 21-megabyte scan last month and wants the same distinction kept. The chunk size should be 8 megabytes, and the simultaneous upload setting should be 2 jobs. That's two jobs at once, not two files total.

Numbered section for the checks before saving:
1. Confirm that the shared Field Desk account is selected and that the personal browser profile has not silently changed the uploader account.
2. Check that the incoming, sent, and staging paths point to the blue drive and that staging is the folder already on disk.
3. Compare the certificate name and office gateway address against the connection card in the top drawer.
4. Check that the file limit says 680 megabytes per file and the daily allowance says 12 gigabytes.
5. Verify the 28-file job cap and the three allowed suffixes without adding ZIP files.
6. Try the resume behavior with one file over 20 megabytes and one at or under 20 megabytes, but do not send either test to the live archive. Use the local sample folder for that check. If the test window asks for a destination, stop and ask me before choosing one.

I would like the first setup pass done after the scanner finishes its morning batch. The batch is usually finished by 10:30, but if it is still running then, wait until it is done rather than opening the archive folder while the scanner is writing into it. Please save a screenshot of the settings page in the team notebook under Uploader Checks, and write down the time shown by the desktop clock when you take it. Don't include any customer documents in the screenshot. The page should show the profile name, the retry setting, and the resume option. If the page has to scroll, use two screenshots instead of shrinking the display scale. I can review the screenshots later today and compare them with the paper setup card.

There is one detail from the desk conversation that matters for the sender label. Jo said, “Use the shared Field Desk wording so the evening staff can recognize it,” and then corrected herself: “Not evening staff; I mean the weekend staff because they cover the archive desk on Saturday.” Keep the sender field as Field Desk Archive anyway, and don't change it to weekend archive. The weekend staff need the same sender label as everyone else. If the reply address is rejected by the form, don't substitute my address; just leave that field unchanged and tell me what message the form shows. Also, if the certificate prompt says the certificate is expired, do not click through the warning. The certificate on our card is meant to be used until November 30, 2025, and I want to check with the network team if the prompt gives a different date.

For the handoff, leave the uploader window open on the connection profile page, but do not start a real transfer. Do not clear the existing history because there are two completed entries from Monday that I need to compare with the index. Leave the local sample files where they are after the test, and tell me whether the test showed a resume option for the 21-megabyte file and a restart for the 19-megabyte file. Don't say that the configuration is finished just because the settings page was saved; I still need to check the screenshots and the certificate prompt if one appeared. The note on the paper card says the archive desk meets on Thursday. I first said Thursday—not Thursday, I mean Friday—so use Friday for any calendar note, and don't change the uploader schedule since there is no automatic schedule configured yet. Please send me the setup note and the screenshot location when you are done with this pass."}]
